analysis.title: UBS Futures Monday Market Preview
key_insights: Risk sentiment fell sharply Friday as anxiety over the viability of the AI trade became a broad positioning unwind. The S&P 500 fell 3.70% to 6,910.39 and entered a technical correction, its worst week since the April 2025 tariff rout.
Nasdaq 100 fell 5.61% on Friday. A closely watched chipmaker index fell 11% and Nvidia fell 14% after a Reuters report that US regulators were investigating its accounting practices.
Nvidia shares hit their lowest level since June 2025 despite beating estimates and raising its outlook in its first results since Jensen Huang's resignation.
Anthropic's record IPO first supported sentiment, but its first-day surge partly reversed and fed a reassessment of AI-linked valuations and positioning.
Equity volatility rose to its highest level since April 2025, and the risk-off move spread to metals, Bitcoin and emerging markets.
US Treasuries rallied in a bull steepening, with yields 10bp to 15bp lower, 2s10s about 2bp wider and 5s30s about 5bp wider. The US 10-year was near 4.92%, down 12bp on the day.
Traders stopped fully pricing a quarter-point Fed hike in December. Governor Cook said inflation remained 'unacceptably high' and the FOMC 'does not have the luxury to wait.'
European bonds followed Treasuries higher. The Bund 10-year fell 10bp to 3.30% and the UK 2-year gilt fell 8bp to 5.23%. ECB's Nagel said the ECB should hike next month.

European equities had their worst week since April 2025, with the Stoxx 600 down 2.00% Friday. Tech had its largest weekly decline in over six years, and rotation moved into defensives such as personal care, food and healthcare.
Copper was heading for one of its worst weeks in a decade on AI-related demand concerns. Brent held below $92, down about 4% on the week and a third straight weekly decline.

APAC setup is defensive. SPI futures closed 49 points lower at 8,556 on volume 138% of the 10-day average, E-mini S&P was 304.8bp below the Australian cash close, and Japan's partial holiday may thin liquidity and add gap risk.
Preliminary November PMIs from India, Europe, the UK and US are the next macro test of whether growth assumptions validate Friday's positioning-led move.

market_movers.rationale: Shares fell 14% on a Reuters report of a US regulatory probe into accounting practices. They hit the lowest since June 2025 despite a beat and raised outlook.

sector_views.rationale: AI-led positioning unwind drove the chipmaker index down 11%. Tech had its largest weekly decline in over six years in Europe.
Investors accelerated rotation into defensive sectors.
Copper was heading for one of its worst weeks in a decade on AI-related demand concerns.

earnings_insights: Nvidia beat estimates and raised its outlook in its first results since Jensen Huang's resignation (figures not given in report). Shares still fell to their lowest since June 2025.

crypto_views: Bitcoin weakened as part of the cross-asset risk-off move alongside equities, metals and emerging markets.
risk_factors: Further AI-linked positioning unwind and valuation reassessment.
Thin Japanese holiday liquidity could amplify price moves and gap risk.
Geopolitical escalation in Poland and Ukraine, and possible renewed US strikes on Iran.
Persistent inflation and Fed or ECB hawkishness, with a December hike still possible.
vol_and_positioning: Equity volatility rose to its highest level since April 2025.
Crowded AI and technology exposures unwound, and positioning rather than data drove the move.
Overnight SPI volume was 20,862 contracts, 138% of the 10-day average of 15,112.5.
Friday AS51 traded value was AUD9.305 billion, 122.3% of its 10-day average.
Cross-asset correlations shifted toward risk reduction, with equities, metals, Bitcoin and EM down while DM sovereigns rallied.
geopolitical: A Russian incursion into Polish airspace refocused attention on the war in Ukraine, and Poland's WIG20 fell 4.5%.
Traders weigh possible renewed US strikes on Iran against signs of ample global crude supply.
